summary: Gregory P. A. Levine works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University before becoming Associate Professor of Art and Architecture of Japan and Buddhist Visual Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2003.

Gregory Price Grieve specializes in religious and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from San Francisco State University and the University of Chicago. He lectured at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

Gregory Schopen, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, earned degrees from Black Hills State, McMaster, and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at Indiana, UT Austin, and UCLA (1999-2019).

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Moscow State University under George de Roerich. He held longtime posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Moscow State University, and the Imperial Academy of Sciences.
Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indologist and historian who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Munich. She subsequently served as a professor there from 1978 to 1991.

Gu Jiegang was an expert in history, archaeology, and sinology who studied at Peking University under Taiyan Zhang and Shih Hu. He later held posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from SOAS, University of London, under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He became an assistant professor at The University of Hong Kong around 2003.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from 1986 to 2004 and as a professor at Shanghai Normal University from around 2004 to 2018.
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and was appointed professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bonn, Münster, and Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner and Michael Hahn. After fellowships in India and Japan, she became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.
Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral studies at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Gudō Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Renpō Niwa. He later lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya, attested in 1991 and 2008.

Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He served as department head at University College, Colombo, and Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Peradeniya.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Stig Wikander. She held a post at Uppsala University from around 1978 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from 1926 to 1933 and held a post there from 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, and trained under Sheng Yen. He is attested as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery in 2013.
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who trained under Sheng Yen and earned a PhD from Rissho University under doctoral supervisor Kenyu Mitomo.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar with degrees from Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught at Baring Union Christian College and Columbia before holding an endowed chair at UC Santa Barbara (1999-2015).
